summary: Christine Mollier specializes in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Kristofer Schipper and Michel Soymié (1989–1995), served as a CNRS researcher (1989–1995; attested 2006, 2014 as Director), and was Numata Visiting Professor at the University of Chicago.

Christmas Humphreys worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Malvern College (~1914–1919) and Trinity Hall, Cambridge (~1919–1922), and served as President of the Buddhist Society from around 1924 to 1983.

Christoph Anderl works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed an MA at the University of Vienna (~1989–1995) and a PhD under Christoph Harbsmeier at the University of Oslo (~1997–2004), becoming a permanent member at Ghent University around 2012.

Christoph Cüppers is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg (~1974–1983) under Lambert Schmithausen, Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, and Albrecht Wezler. From ~1993 to 2013, he served as Director of the Lumbini International Research Institute.

Christoph Emmrich specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Heidelberg University under Axel Michaels by 2004, held an attested post at Heidelberg in 2001, and is attested as an Assistant Professor at the University of Toronto in 2026.

Christoph Harbsmeier works in Sinology and linguistics. He studied at Merton College, Oxford (~1966–1973) and the University of Copenhagen (~1973–1981). He held posts at Universiti Sains Malaysia (1973–1976) and the University of Oslo, where he became Professor in 1980.

Christoph Kleine specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his degrees and Habilitation at the University of Marburg, and held professorships at the University of Munich (2004–2008) and Leipzig University (appointed 2008).

Christoph Theodosius Walther was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied theology at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1720 and served as a missionary with the Danish-Halle Mission from around 1725 to 1739.

Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf worked in history and archaeology. He earned his doctorate and Habilitation at the University of Vienna and studied at the LSE. He was Professor at Osmania University (1945) and held the Chair of Asian Anthropology at the University of London (1951–1976).

Christophe Jaffrelot specializes in Indology. He studied at Sciences Po (~1985–1991) under Jean Leca, took posts at Sciences Po and CNRS in ~1991, and became Professor of Indian Politics and Sociology at King's College London around 2015.
Christophe Vielle is an Indologist. He held a professorship at the Catholic University of Louvain (attested 2009–2013) and is attested as an Associate member at Ghent University in 2026.

Christopher Andreas Holmboe worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Oslo (~1814–1818) and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Armand-Pierre Caussin de Perceval in 1821, later serving as Reader (1822) and Professor of Oriental Languages (1828) at Oslo.

Christopher Byrne is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at McGill University (attested 2015), where he studied under Grace S. Fong, G. Victor Sōgen Hori, and Robin D. S. Yates.
Christopher D. Emms works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has been a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University under the supervision of Shayne Clarke (attested 2012–2026).

Christopher Framarin works in philosophy and Indology. He earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (-2001) and a PhD at the University of New Mexico (-2005), and held faculty posts at the University of Calgary (attested 2014, 2026).
Christopher Hatchell specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia, where he was mentored by David Germano.

Christopher I. Beckwith works in Tibetology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Ohio State and Indiana University Bloomington under Helmut Hoffmann and Thubten Jigme Norbu, joining Indiana University's faculty in ~1978 and becoming Professor in 1982.

Christopher Ives specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He served as Assistant Professor of Religion at the University of Puget Sound (~1987–2001) and later became professor and chair of religious studies at Stonehill College (~2001).

Christopher Jon Jensen works in religious studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of Saskatchewan, Kyoto University, and McMaster University (PhD -2018), where his doctoral supervisor was James A. Benn.

Christopher Kelley is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Columbia University and has taught at Columbia University, The New School, and Brooklyn College.
